standard_prerequisites.name: The category of sheaves on the small Zariski site of quasi-coherent modules agrees with the quasi-coherent modules on the ringed space, and the categories of modules agree, so the two derived categories are equivalent
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the equivalence between the first two categories of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The equivalence of ringed topoi between the site of affines and the Zariski site induces an equivalence of module categories that preserves the quasi-coherent subcategories because intrinsicness of that notion
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the equivalence between the second and third categories.

standard_prerequisites.name: The comparison lemma for adequate modules produces an equivalence of derived categories from a morphism of ringed sites once four conditions on a basis and a subcategory of presheaves are checked
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the equivalence between the last two categories once its hypotheses are verified.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-coherent modules on the affine site are exactly the presheaves compatible with localizing the ring of sections, and they are also exactly the quasi-coherent modules in the chaotic topology
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the two descriptions of the subcategory to which the comparison lemma is applied.

core_obligations: For the last two categories: since the ring maps between affine opens are flat, the equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on the affine site and the abelian category of the statement is a special case of the flat cartesian quasi-coherent comparison (proof lines 11014-11018).

Identify the modules on the Zariski site with the modules on the ringed space by the standard remark, and check that quasi-coherent modules correspond under that identification, which gives the equivalence between the first and second categories (proof lines 11019-11025).

Use the equivalence of ringed topoi between the site of affines and the Zariski site to get an equivalence of module categories, and observe that the notion of quasi-coherence is intrinsic, so the equivalence preserves the quasi-coherent subcategories; this gives the equivalence between the second and third categories (proof lines 11026-11032).

For the equivalence between the third and fourth categories, apply the comparison lemma for adequate modules to the morphism from the affine site to the affine space, taking the basis of all affine opens and the full subcategory of presheaves whose sections localize correctly (proof lines 11033-11044).

Identify that subcategory with the quasi-coherent modules on the Zariski topology using the descent statement, and with the quasi-coherent modules in the chaotic topology using the intrinsicness statement, so that the comparison lemma gives the equivalence on the derived categories (proof lines 11045-11058).

Verify the four conditions of the comparison lemma: every object of the subcategory is a Zariski sheaf; the subcategory is a weak Serre subcategory, which follows because it is the category of quasi-coherent modules; every object has a covering by members of the basis, trivially since the basis is everything; and the higher cohomology of quasi-coherent modules on affines vanishes, which is the affine vanishing statement (proof lines 11059-11089).
proof_roadmap: The equivalence for the flat comparison between the last two categories (proof lines 11014-11018).
Zariski site versus ringed space, and the intrinsicness of quasi-coherence for the affine site (proof lines 11019-11032).
Set up the comparison lemma with the chosen basis and subcategory (proof lines 11033-11058).
Verify the four conditions and conclude (proof lines 11059-11089).
